newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses at record highs, dollar holds firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses at record highs, dollar holds firm.

text.p: Bourses in London, Frankfurt and Paris all hit record levels on Monday and already bullish sentiment in Europe was underlined when Wall Street turned positive in early trading.

Dealers said profit-taking was dampening rises at these high levels. But confidence was boosted by the continuing bull-run on Wall Street plus the firming dollar -- good for European exports -- and the feeling that interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic are on hold, at least for the time being.
On currency markets the dollar held firm against the mark and was slightly lower against the yen in afternoon trading after recovering from lows in Asia.
The overnight lows were sparked by signals from the weekend meeting of finance chiefs of the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations that they may try to halt its rise.
The dollar, which fell sharply in early Asian trading to just over the key 120 yen level, had bounced back to 122.65 by 1515 GMT in Europe, not far short of its Friday New York close of 123.10.
Against the mark it was at around 1.6555 by 1515 gmt, still short of its 1.6610 Friday New York close.

In a statement released after a meeting on Saturday, the G7 nations -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States -- signalled their desire for stability in the foreign exchange markets by saying that their currencies were no longer misaligned in a major way.
The accord was good news for Japan, which has grown increasingly worried about the dollar's sharp climb against the yen -- a massive 55 percent in less than two years.

Traders and analysts said there was a common thread running through the various comments surrounding the meeting which suggested dollar gains were welcome but further gains from here would be monitored closely.

"The tone of the comments seem to say the dollar may have come just a little too far, too fast," said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch. While not overtly negative for the dollar, that may now create a bit more of a two-way market."

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Monday that the current dollar rate of about 122.50 yen best reflected the G7 call for market stability.

"We have been seeking a stable foreign exchange market and have said that excessive fluctuations were undesireable, which was stated in the G7 statement. The currency rate today reflects that and is at 122.50 yen," he said in Tokyo.
However, some analysts said the G7 may, ironically, risk increasing currency volatility by attempting to fine-tune the major exchange rates.

On the equity front leading London shares were holding in record territory in early afternoon trading, fuelled by strong gains in the bank, insurance and financial sectors and the higher opening in New York.
By 1515 gmt, the FTSE 100 was up 15.3 points at 4,323.1, just off the record peak of 4,330.0 set earlier in the day.
The British bank sector rallied, with several stocks climbing to records on expectations the sector will report strong results, dealers said.
Elsewhere, shares in British Airways Plc jumped 12p to 598-1/2 after the airline delivered record third quarter profits.
Dealers said trading was edgy, however, with some investors taking profits after Friday's fresh record stock index rise.
"Now that the FTSE is above 4,300 people are a bit nervous. It's not too surprising that we're seeing a few people lock in some profits," the head of trading at a large investment bank said.

In Frankfurt German shares ended bourse trade sharply higher before Wall Street opened. The main German DAX index of floor trading closed at a record 3,184.36 points, up 46.35. After New York opened for business the IBIS DAX index of electronic trading continued to firm to well above its previous highest level.
Trading was more subdued on the Paris bourse. Nevertheless the CAC-40 index was up about a quarter of a percent by mid-afternoon, slightly above its previous trading high.
CURRENCIES AT 1515 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6555 marks and 122.65 yen compared with 1.6725 marks and 124.45 yen in late European trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1515 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 15.3 at 4,323.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 7.14 at 2,604.78.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 46.35 at 3,184.36.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at 340.4, compared with its London close on Friday of $340.45. Silver was at $4.93.
